title: sticky-segment-routing-with-variant-fallback-and-cost-prioritization
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood needs deterministic routing semantics for cohorts during canary/A-B experiments while simultaneously respecting region selection, tier routing (e.g., premium vs. standard), and automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants when capacity or SLA constraints trigger degradations. Current rollout behavior is either sticky at the request level (too volatile) or global (not cohort-aware), which leads to noisy metrics and poor graduation signals during gradual rollouts.

Problem statement:
- We need session/cohort affinity that:
  * Is deterministic and reproducible across requests for the same session or identity key.
  * Respects routing preference hierarchy (region -> tier -> model variant).
  * Allows controlled degrade to fallback variants (eg. quantized / smaller models) with predictable, observable impact.
- Rollout semantics (canary weights, A/B splits) must interact with affinity in a way that avoids noisy churn when users cross regions or when capacity changes occur.

Goals:
1) Provide a "sticky segment" routing primitive: deterministic hashing + TTL-based affinity keyed by identity/session/cohort.
2) Introduce a cost-prioritization policy layer that can prefer lower-cost compatible variants for lower-tier traffic while still honoring canary assignments for a target percentage of users.
3) Define safe graduation and rollback signals (SLO-driven) for canaries that account for cohort stickiness and fallback noise.
4) Emit observability signals (per-cohort latency/cost/quality deltas) to Console and Optimize so PMs/DS can evaluate.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Affinity mechanism: deterministic 64-bit hash over (routing_key || cohort_seed) -> map to routing buckets. TTL attached to bucket assignment (default 24h). Affinity update on identity change or explicit session reset. Provide a "segmented affinity" option that groups by coarse geography first to reduce cross-region churn.
- Routing precedence: evaluate in order: 1) pinned version (if present and valid), 2) cohort-assigned rollout bucket (canary/A-B), 3) configured tier preference (customer plan), 4) region preferred pool, 5) global fallback.
- Cost-prioritization layer: rule engine that can annotate certain buckets as "cost-optimized". When enabled, for non-canary cohort buckets prefer compatible variants (eg. 8-bit quantized) unless the cohort is in the explicit canary cohort. This engine must be declarative and limited by capacity policies so it cannot breach SLA.
- Fallback variants: define variant compatibility sets and degrade policies (soft degrade vs forced fallback). Soft degrade: route new requests to smaller variant but keep pinned sessions on original variant until TTL expiry. Forced fallback: immediate switch for non-pinned traffic during region outage or capacity exhaustion.
- Canary/A-B interaction: when creating a canary with weight W, select W% of cohort hashes as canary-assigned. If cohort affinity TTL is active, a user that falls into control/experiment bucket remains there until TTL ends or explicit migration is triggered. Ensure deterministic mapping across rollout changes by using a stable hash ring and epoched salt when we want to rebalance.

Detailed acceptance criteria:
- API: new rollout object supports fields: cohort_seed, affinity_ttl_seconds, cost_priority_mode (off|soft|strict), region_grouping_mode (coarse|fine).
- Determinism: given same routing_key, cohort_seed, and salt, assignment is identical across nodes.
- Affinity TTL honored: pinned sessions keep original assignment for TTL duration; documented behavior for pin drains.
- Cost policy respects canary assignments: canary cohort must be able to opt out of cost-prioritization automatically.
- Observability: Console shows cohort-level breakdown with tokens, latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, and fallback rate.
- Rollout safety: automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold (configurable) or if latency/cost SLOs breach by configured delta.

Implementation plan (tasks):
- Engine: implement segmented affinity hashing + TTL store (ENG-34102 will be used for affinity storage primitives).
- Router: augment routing resolver to evaluate precedence and cost-priority rules; add variant compatibility registry.
- Control plane: extend rollout API with cohort_seed, affinity_ttl_seconds, and cost_policy options.
- Console: add cohort panel and a fallback-rate chart.
- E2E tests: deterministic maps, TTL expiration tests, forced fallback scenarios, canary graduation/rollback flows.

Metrics & monitoring:
- New metrics: cohort_assignments_total, cohort_fallbacks_total, cohort_cost_tokens, cohort_latency_ms_p50_p95, cohort_quality_regressions.
- Alerts: high fallback rate (>5% sustained) for >5m, canary quality delta > configured threshold, affinity store error rate spike.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: stale affinity leading to delayed rollbacks during incidents. Mitigation: provide an emergency "flush affinity" control in Console and allow per-rollout override to disable TTL during emergencies.
- Risk: complexity in cost-prioritization causing unpredictable economics. Mitigation: start with "soft" mode where cost hints are advisory and surface expected cost delta in Console before enabling strict mode.

Open questions:
- Default affinity TTL: should be 24h or shorter for chat-heavy products? (PM preference requested).
- Should pinned-version semantics override forced fallback during severe capacity constraints? (ops safety vs. correctness trade-off).

Deliverables:
- Router + Control plane changes (code + migration docs).
- Console cohort observability view and a rollout preview that shows expected cohort assignments and cost delta.
- Runbook for emergency affinity flush and canary rollback playbook.

2025-02-25 - Marcus Huang: Spike complete. Implemented segmented hashing prototype. Found edge-case when cohort_seed changes mid-rollout - added note to prevent salt rotations during active canary. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4987
